scope: Only add ticket/take/seating/sofa/ordering to published child-loader capability. Prior airship/radio/curiosity retained. No game, registry, menu, train, age, bridge, readiness or sandbox changes.
method: Anonymous actual canonical HTTPS hub and independently live registered children in Chromium. Real menu card launches in 60 cold/cached cases at six sizes. No route interception, fake parent, forged messages, relaxed security launch flags or browser security bypass. Read-only message listener records real child events. Touch emulation on phone/Duo; keyboard Enter and reduced motion on desktop. Not physical iPad/Safari hardware.

publication.shaLimitation: Public sourceVersion remains inherited 50b7764, not the current Git SHA. New build ID plus canonical changed-layer checks establish rollout behavior, not exact deployed SHA.

summary.realWin: take: authoritative visible arithmetic answered; Correct feedback and Next adventure pressed; same prepared iframe promoted
summary.storyReveal: All five actual child intro stories observed separately after readiness and loader completion.

limitations: Child ready may precede loader dismissal: seating/sofa/ordering emitted ready about 28–2634ms in several cases, and some cached ordering captures were already ready. Hello-to-ready is NOT claimed to equal loader-visible duration; a guaranteed 3-second painted-child duration is not proven for every child/cached path. No child source was changed.
Seating initial pre-ready captures sometimes caught its unpainted base. Additional painted screenshot shows actual approved artwork but is after ready; do not treat it as before-ready proof.

Seating Next was confirmed in an earlier real run with identical reserved element, but later repeats caught another child loading phase after Begin and had no visible Next at sampling time; per-run data retained.
Only taking-away win was played here; ticket/seating/sofa/ordering wins not rerun. Their real Next controls were exercised where available.

20-second timeout/retry/back, pre-ready Next refusal, forged/hidden message refusal, release replacement and error retry are simulated component regressions in this turn, not a forced production outage.
No physical device audible/touch verification. No claim of complete security assessment: basic scan reported no issues; deep code analysis did not run.
